subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 38-year-old man with treatment-resistant depression has been taking a nonselective monoamine oxidase inhibitor. At a dinner party he eats aged cheese and cured sausage and within an hour develops an occipital headache, palpitations, and sweating, with a blood pressure of 220/115 mm Hg. He is treated in the emergency department and recovers.
question: Which of the following best explains this reaction?

options.text: Tyramine directly stimulates beta-adrenergic receptors on vascular smooth muscle
Monoamine oxidase inhibition increases catecholamine biosynthesis in the adrenal medulla
Tyramine is not degraded by monoamine oxidase, is taken up into adrenergic terminals, and displaces stored norepinephrine
Tyramine inhibits catechol-O-methyltransferase and blocks norepinephrine degradation
Tyramine acts as an antagonist at presynaptic alpha-2 receptors and reduces norepinephrine release

explanation_correct: Aged cheese, cured meats, and fermented products contain tyramine, an indirect sympathomimetic that is normally degraded by monoamine oxidase in the gut wall and liver. When a nonselective monoamine oxidase inhibitor is present, tyramine reaches adrenergic nerve terminals, enters them through the uptake transporter, and displaces norepinephrine from vesicular stores into the synaptic cleft, causing a hypertensive crisis often called the cheese reaction.

explanation_incorrect.A: Tyramine has little direct receptor activity; its pressor effect requires uptake into terminals and release of stored norepinephrine.
explanation_incorrect.B: Monoamine oxidase inhibition reduces catecholamine degradation rather than increasing medullary catecholamine synthesis.
explanation_incorrect.D: Catechol-O-methyltransferase is not the target of tyramine; tyramine increases norepinephrine availability by displacement rather than by inhibiting methylation.
explanation_incorrect.E: Tyramine increases rather than decreases norepinephrine release, and alpha-2 agonists are the agents that reduce release.

educationalObjective: The cheese reaction occurs because tyramine escapes monoamine oxidase degradation and displaces stored norepinephrine, producing severe hypertension in patients taking nonselective monoamine oxidase inhibitors.
